import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def maxSubarraySum_precond (seq : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  0 < seq.length ∧ seq.length ≤ 100000
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def spec_sum (seq : List Int) (i j : Nat) : Int :=
  ((seq.drop i).take (j - i)).foldl (fun acc x => acc + x) 0

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def intervalPairs (n : Nat) : Finset (Nat × Nat) :=
  (((Finset.range (n + 1)).product (Finset.range (n + 1))).filter
    (fun p : Nat × Nat => p.1 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ n))

lemma mem_intervalPairs {n i j : Nat} :
    (i, j) ∈ intervalPairs n ↔ i ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h' : (i < n + 1 ∧ j < n + 1) ∧ (i ≤ j ∧ j ≤ n) := by
      simpa [intervalPairs] using h
    exact h'.2
  · intro h
    have hi : i < n + 1 := Nat.lt_succ_of_le (le_trans h.1 h.2)
    have hj : j < n + 1 := Nat.lt_succ_of_le h.2
    simp [intervalPairs, hi, hj, h.1, h.2]

def subarraySums (seq : List Int) : Finset Int :=
  (intervalPairs seq.length).image (fun p : Nat × Nat => spec_sum seq p.1 p.2)

lemma subarraySums_nonempty (seq : List Int) : (subarraySums seq).Nonempty := by
  refine ⟨spec_sum seq 0 0, ?_⟩
  unfold subarraySums
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr
    ⟨(0, 0), mem_intervalPairs.mpr ⟨le_rfl, Nat.zero_le seq.length⟩, rfl⟩
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def maxSubarraySum (seq : List Int) (h_precond : maxSubarraySum_precond (seq)) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  (subarraySums seq).max' (subarraySums_nonempty seq)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def maxSubarraySum_postcond (seq : List Int) (result: Int) (h_precond : maxSubarraySum_precond (seq)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ i j : Nat, i ≤ j → j ≤ seq.length → spec_sum seq i j ≤ result) ∧
  (∃ i j : Nat, i ≤ j ∧ j ≤ seq.length ∧ spec_sum seq i j = result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem maxSubarraySum_postcond_satisfied (seq: List Int) (h_precond : maxSubarraySum_precond (seq)) :
    maxSubarraySum_postcond (seq) (maxSubarraySum (seq) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  constructor
  · intro i j hij hj
    have hmem : spec_sum seq i j ∈ subarraySums seq := by
      unfold subarraySums
      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr
        ⟨(i, j), mem_intervalPairs.mpr ⟨hij, hj⟩, rfl⟩
    simpa [maxSubarraySum] using
      (Finset.le_max' (subarraySums seq) (spec_sum seq i j) hmem)
  · have hmem : maxSubarraySum seq h_precond ∈ subarraySums seq := by
      unfold maxSubarraySum
      exact Finset.max'_mem (subarraySums seq) (subarraySums_nonempty seq)
    unfold subarraySums at hmem
    rcases Finset.mem_image.mp hmem with ⟨p, hp, hp_eq⟩
    refine ⟨p.1, p.2, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact (mem_intervalPairs.mp hp).1
    · exact (mem_intervalPairs.mp hp).2
    · exact hp_eq
  -- !benchmark @end proof

analysis:
The implementation does not use Kadane’s algorithm. Instead, it explicitly constructs every valid interval pair `(i, j)`, maps each pair to its subarray sum, stores those sums in a `Finset`, and selects the maximum using the library function `Finset.max'`.

Although this computes a value satisfying the stated postcondition and the proof contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or empty body, it violates the natural-language requirement to implement Kadane’s algorithm. Kadane’s algorithm should process the sequence incrementally while maintaining a best sum ending at the current position and a global best sum, normally in linear time. This solution enumerates quadratically many intervals and repeatedly computes sums, making it substantially less efficient. It also delegates the final maximum computation to an existing verified library operation rather than implementing the required algorithm from scratch.

Therefore, compilation and proof success do not make it semantically compliant with the requested implementation approach.
